findings.title: Denial cache key does not include identity type, causing cross-identity collisions
findings.body: The denial cache key is built without the identity type. For anonymous users the parsed userUID is "0", and for render service the parsed userUID is also "0". Since the key does not differentiate between these identity types, a denial entry cached for an anonymous user can be returned for a render service request for the same action/name/parent, and vice versa. This can cause incorrect authorization decisions (false denials). The key should include checkReq.IdentityType to separate identities.

findings.title: Denial cache key concatenation can cause collisions between different resources
findings.body: The function userPermDenialCacheKey builds a key by concatenating namespace, userUID, action, name, and parent with underscores, with no escaping or delimiter that cannot appear in the values. For example, name="foo_bar" and parent="" produces the same key as name="foo" and parent="bar". Such collisions can cause a denial cached for one resource to be incorrectly applied to a different resource, leading to false access denials. Use a safe encoding (e.g., length-prefixing, hashing, or a non-ambiguous delimiter) or a structured key builder.

findings.title: Denial cache entries are not invalidated when permissions are granted, causing temporary false denials
findings.body: When a check results in a deny, the service stores a denial entry in permDenialCache with TTL 30 seconds. This cache is checked first on subsequent requests and is never invalidated when permissions are added or the resource is created. A user who previously attempted to access a resource that did not exist or for which they lacked permission will have a denial entry for that resource key. If the resource is then created or the user is granted permission, they will continue to be denied for up to 30 seconds because the stale denial entry is returned before checking the permission cache or database. This can cause the very problem the PR aims to fix (immediate access to newly created dashboards/folders) for resources with previously attempted names. The denial cache should be cleared on permission changes or the TTL should be very short, or denials should only be cached when the resource is known to exist.
